items.title: Turn protocol propagation into an executable compatibility court at the real startup entry points.
items.why: The latest canonical propagation silently replaced working capability-map fallback and brief presentation semantics. Existing unit tests covered shared helpers but not renderer wiring, so startup reported 0/0 capabilities, malformed Genius/Human Pressure boxes, and misleading variable-cost language. It also created internal status/forecast artifacts that are currently unignored in a public repo.
items.recipe: Keep the repaired shared capability-map precedence and flat-rate presentation; make render-startup-brief consume normalizeGeniusBlock/renderHumanPressureBlock instead of duplicate logic; add an integration fixture that runs the actual renderer against adversarial propagated input and validates the brief; add a bounded startup acceptance command covering capability count/provenance, brief schema, cost semantics, and public-artifact policy; ignore only generated context/SIGNALS.md and portfolio/compiled artifacts. Fail closed without reading or printing values.

L1.recipe: Retain the startup repairs and ignore the two generated private artifact paths.

L2.recipe: Wire the renderer to shared box helpers and add real-entrypoint regression fixtures.

L3.recipe: Ship one self-validating propagation acceptance receipt spanning secrets provenance, rendered boxes, flat-rate cost semantics, and public-boundary artifact policy.

items.title: Resolve weapon progression into an all-open arsenal with earned mastery rather than contradictory access locks.
items.why: The latest decision exposes all twelve primaries before deployment, but the custom builder still locks later weapons and the runway promises a next weapon unlock. The builder also passes the full career object into a numeric level function, forcing level one. Players can bypass those locks through the primary selector, so the gate creates confusion rather than progression.
items.recipe: Define one arsenal progression contract: every primary is selectable; WEAPON_UNLOCK_LEVELS becomes mastery-license levels that award visible proficiency/evolution/cosmetic status without access denial; replace nextWeapon with nextMastery in the runway; update level-up analytics and copy; remove disabled weapon options while retaining earned-state badges; add contract tests proving every pre-run/in-run surface allows all twelve and every mastery threshold remains deterministic. Record the resolution against the S55/S134 decisions.

L2.recipe: Remove contradictory access locks and rename runway/telemetry language to mastery.

L3.recipe: Ship a versioned cross-surface arsenal contract with earned badges, migration-safe storage, analytics reason codes, and exact all-twelve/threshold fixtures.

items.title: Collapse the menu's two recommendation systems into one reason-coded, executable next-run plan.

Route every action through one exhaustive dispatcher with safe fallback; preserve aim-check precedence and challenge/daily semantics; launch Gauntlet immediately using its weekly seed/loadout. Add first-run, input, rival, daily, upgrade, mission, revenge, play-now, and Gauntlet fixtures plus keyboard/controller accessible CTA coverage.

L1.recipe: Attach the existing recommended action to a handler and make Gauntlet start immediately.

L2.recipe: Unify action priorities and payloads while retaining all current destinations and analytics.

items.title: Capture reproducible production Lighthouse evidence for HomeV2 and the legacy route without pretending it is funnel data.
items.why: The HomeV1 retirement gate has remained Lighthouse-and-funnel blocked for months. Lighthouse performance is agent-executable against production, but there is no checked-in, source-hash-bound comparison receipt. Funnel conversion and the required observation window remain genuinely external.

skipped.reason: No five-session receipt-backed playtest or production distribution supports changing damage, health, spawn, cooldown, reward, or progression pacing.
The core loop is already deep; progression truth and return-path execution outrank another weapon, mode, enemy, or metagame.
Local deterministic intelligence is deep and a hosted model would add variable per-user cost without demonstrated need.
Guest play is intentional; the local auth plan triggers only at traffic or paid-tier thresholds and must converge on Obelisk rather than silently shipping project-local identity.
This mission can capture production Lighthouse, but 48-hour funnel evidence and the recorded threshold remain absent; deletion would fabricate the gate.
Project-scoped credentials are unproven; a generic available credential is not authority to mutate another project's telemetry.
No Zoho alias delivery and reply-as-alias receipt exists.
Automation cannot replace physical PWA/gamepad/full-run media passes or direct human/AI rendered-pixel judgment.
Publication, exact external proofs, and explicit founder approval remain distinct from engineering completion.
The checker parse error is Studio Ops-owned; this repo will ship signed Ark evidence instead of editing a sibling tree.
